claims.text: The untreated alloy has a typical coarse-grained microstructure.
The untreated alloy has relatively high friction and wear under standard operating conditions.
Plasma nitriding in an NH3-rich atmosphere at 500–600 °C for 10–20 hours will form a nitrided surface layer on Nb40Ta25Ti15Hf15Zr5.
Optimized temperature profiles or duration adjustments will produce a ductile, adherent gradient nitrided layer.
The nitrided layer will contain hard metal-nitride phases.
The nitrided layer will contain intrinsically low-shear, lubricious metal-nitride phases.
The nitrided layer will transition gradually into the untreated bulk alloy.
Formation of metal-nitride compounds will increase surface hardness.
The gradient interface will minimize adhesive wear.
The gradient nitrided surface will provide a robust, self-lubricating contact that adapts to variable thermal and mechanical stresses.
Optimized plasma nitriding will reduce the coefficient of friction of the alloy to below 0.3 relative to the untreated control.
Optimized plasma nitriding will reduce wear rate by approximately one order of magnitude relative to the untreated control.
The friction and wear improvements will persist from room temperature to the upper service-temperature limits typical of refractory applications.
The treatment will remain effective if nitriding parameters prevent excessive brittleness, delamination, and microcracking during repeated thermal and mechanical cycling.
Long-term stability under extensive service and thermal cycling is uncertain and depends on maintaining layer ductility and adhesion.
